back: Angle subtended at centre by an arc of length equal to the radius: θ = l/r. Full circle = 2π radians.
l = rθ with θ in RADIANS. Convert degrees first, always.
Degrees × π/180; radians × 180/π. Cancel fractions before multiplying: 240° = 4π/3.
sin(2nπ + x) = sin x, cos(2nπ + x) = cos x, n ∈ Z. Both repeat every 2π.
sin x = 0 ⇔ x = nπ. cos x = 0 ⇔ x = (2n+1)π/2. These decide tan/cot domains too.
cosec = 1/sin (x ≠ nπ); sec = 1/cos, tan = sin/cos (x ≠ odd π/2 multiples); cot = cos/sin (x ≠ nπ).
sin²+cos² = 1; 1+tan² = sec²; 1+cot² = cosec². Divide the first by sin² or cos² to get the others.
cos(–x) = cos x (even); sin(–x) = –sin x (odd). Reciprocals inherit: sec even, cosec/tan/cot odd.
I: All +; II: only Sin (+cosec); III: only Tan (+cot); IV: only Cos (+sec).
sin, cos: ℝ → [–1,1]. cosec, sec: ℝ minus poles → (–∞,–1]∪[1,∞). tan, cot: ℝ minus poles → ℝ.
sin, cos, cosec, sec: period 2π. tan, cot: period π.
cos(x±y) = cosxcosy ∓ sinxsiny; sin(x±y) = sinxcosy ± cosxsiny.
(tanx ± tany)/(1 ∓ tanxtany) — valid when none of x, y, x±y is an odd multiple of π/2.
cos2x = cos²−sin² = 2cos²−1 = 1−2sin² = (1−tan²)/(1+tan²); sin2x = 2sinxcosx; tan2x = 2tanx/(1−tan²x).
sin3x = 3sinx − 4sin³x; cos3x = 4cos³x − 3cosx; tan3x = (3tanx − tan³x)/(1 − 3tan²x).
cosx+cosy = 2cos((x+y)/2)cos((x−y)/2); sinx+siny = 2sin((x+y)/2)cos((x−y)/2); differences flip to the other function, cos-difference carries a minus.
2cosxcosy = cos(x+y)+cos(x−y); 2sinxcosy = sin(x+y)+sin(x−y); −2sinxsiny = cos(x+y)−cos(x−y); 2cossiny = sin(x+y)−sin(x−y).
√2 − 1. From tan 2x = 1 forcing y² + 2y − 1 = 0 and taking the positive root.
sin(x/2) takes sign from where x/2 LIVES, not x. Check the quadrant of x/2 before choosing ±.
Huge angle? Subtract the nearest multiple of the period first: 31π/3 − 10π = π/3.
